links.outcome: Trainees' accuracy and sensitivity in detecting ChatGPT-4o hallucinations in simulated clinical questions
links.effect: Mean accuracy of detecting the 87 hallucinations was 55.0%, mean sensitivity (d') 0.39, showing trainees often failed to verify and catch incorrect AI outputs.
links.quote: The mean accuracy of detecting these hallucinations was 55.0%, and the mean sensitivity (d') was 0.39.

links.outcome: Users' ability to detect incorrect AI outputs (hallucinations) from ChatGPT-4o
links.effect: GP trainees detected hallucinations with 55.0% mean accuracy and d' of 0.39; the authors conclude they faced challenges identifying errors, particularly in clinical scenarios.
links.quote: The study concluded that GP trainees faced challenges in identifying ChatGPT-4o's errors, particularly in clinical scenarios.

unlisted_practices: AI literacy and critical thinking education in medical training to improve error detection

screen.reason: Empirically evaluates the ability of GP trainees to act as human reviewers detecting AI hallucinations and errors in clinical education scenarios.
